title: Formal-verification team config
description: Schema for formal-verification.yaml in a repository's convention home (default docs/conventions): version pins and default bounds. Every key is optional; an absent key takes its value from the plugin's defaults.json. Download URLs and checksums are never set here: they come only from the plugin's releases.json, so a version chosen here must have an entry there. scripts/settings.mjs resolves the layers. Contract: docs/adr/0064-home-plugin-customization-in-docs-conventions-yaml.md.

model_checker.description: The TLC model checker jar that /formal-verification:setup apply install-model-checker downloads and checks.

version.description: Release of tla2tools.jar; it must have an entry in the plugin's releases.json.

java.description: The Java that runs TLC. The plugin never installs Java.

min_version.description: Lowest Java major version setup accepts.

distribution.description: The Java distribution setup names in its install hint.

renderer.description: The image renderer, used only when an image of a chart is asked for.

package.description: npm package name of the renderer; package@version must have an entry in the plugin's releases.json.

bounds.description: Default bounds and limits for /formal-verification:chart. A model's run command can pass its own.

chart_states.description: The chart budget in distinct states (--chart-states).

rerun_states.description: After the first break, each TLC run stops at this many distinct states (--rerun-states).

timeout_seconds.description: Wall-clock limit on each Java run; the run's process group is killed past it (--timeout-seconds). At most 2147483, the longest a timer holds.

output_bytes.description: Cap on the bytes one Java run may print; the run is killed past it (--output-bytes).

interval_max.description: An interval with more members than this reaches the view as {lo, hi} instead of a list (--interval-max).

allowed_modules.description: Standard modules a spec may EXTEND or INSTANCE, besides its own (--modules). Modules such as Json read and write files on the machine.
